title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: It's Too Long to Study at University for Four Years, Two Years Are Enough

content_html:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, discussed his educational experience in a recent public interview, candidly stating that dropping out after two years of college was "just right." He believes this growth path is likely to fit many other young people in today's fast-paced technological environment.

Two Years of Study Was Enough to Support Entrepreneurship

Altman admitted that during his two years at Stanford, he had already acquired the core knowledge needed for his subsequent entrepreneurship. If he had spent the remaining two years on campus, the additional practical gains would have been minimal, and the cost-benefit ratio of the time investment would not have been high.

In his view, the traditional four-year university education that has been used for decades may not be the optimal choice in today's technology-driven environment. However, he did not completely negate the value of universities, acknowledging that campuses still provide valuable social settings, allowing people to meet like-minded friends, experience independent living for the first time, and participate in hands-on projects.

The Tradition of "Dropping Out to Start a Business" in the Tech World

Altman himself is a practitioner of this approach—after two years at Stanford in 2005, he voluntarily dropped out and formed a team to start a location-sharing app called Loopt. The product later became one of the first incubated projects of Y Combinator, which led to his long-term association with this legendary incubator. Years later, he even personally took charge of it.

Such views of breaking away from the traditional university path are not new in the Western tech world. His entrepreneurial mentor, Peter Thiel, co-founder of PayPal, has long publicly supported young people skipping the full academic program. His established scholarship directly offers $250,000 in startup funding, encouraging eligible young people to abandon enrollment or take a leave of absence to start practicing earlier.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 在最近的一次公开采访中谈到了他的教育经历，坦诚地表示，大学两年后退学“恰到好处”。 他认为，在当今快节奏的技术环境中，这种成长道路可能适合许多其他年轻人。

两年学习足以支撑创业

奥特曼坦言，在斯坦福的两年时间里，他已经掌握了后续创业所需的核心知识。 如果剩下的两年都在校园里度过，额外的实际收获微乎其微，时间投入的成本效益比也不会很高。

在他看来，沿用了几十年的传统四年制大学教育在当今技术驱动的环境下可能不是最佳选择。 不过，他并没有完全否定大学的价值，承认校园仍然提供有价值的社交环境，让人们结识志同道合的朋友，第一次体验独立生活，参与动手项目。

科技界“辍学创业”的传统

Altman 本人就是这种方法的实践者 - 在 2005 年在斯坦福大学学习两年后，他自愿退学并组建了一个团队，启动了一款名为 Loopt 的位置共享应用程序。 该产品后来成为Y Combinator首批孵化的项目之一，这也让他与这个传奇孵化器产生了长期的联系。 多年后，他甚至亲自主持了这件事。

这种脱离传统大学道路的观点在西方科技界并不新鲜。 他的创业导师、PayPal 联合创始人 Peter Thiel 长期以来一直公开支持年轻人跳过完整的学术课程。 他设立的奖学金直接提供25万美元的启动资金，鼓励符合条件的年轻人放弃入学或请假早点开始实践。
